answer: Identity can be made to age, not just register. Each new key must run a verifiable-delay chain seeded from its own public key across a full season of epochs; the chain is sequential, so renting more machines never shortens the wait. A zephyr of block-hash randomness samples a few keys each round, and any chain with gaps, or a batch whose birth times cluster suspiciously, is slashed and its bond burned. Like nectar that ripens only on the vine, trust is not bought overnight. Cost to an attacker: a bond plus one genuine voyage of elapsed time per fake.
